definition: Localizing which image region a natural-language phrase refers to.
details: Localizing which image region a natural-language phrase refers to. It connects textual spans to visual boxes and underpins referring-expression comprehension and vision-language reasoning.

explainer.lead: Phrase grounding localizes the image region that a natural-language phrase refers to. It matters because it links text spans to visual boxes, enabling referring-expression comprehension and vision-language reasoning.

tiers.eli5: Given a phrase like “the red cup” and a picture, it points to the exact spot in the picture the phrase means.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train models to output bounding boxes aligned to text spans for referring expressions. Pitfall: ambiguous phrases with multiple matching regions need disambiguation beyond the span alone.
tiers.paperLevel: A task connecting textual spans to visual boxes; it underpins referring-expression comprehension and vision-language reasoning. Limits: performance depends on both span and box localization accuracy.

explainer.example: For the sentence “the dog next to the tree,” the system outputs a box around that dog in the photo.
